newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds mostly flat ahead of payrolls.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds mostly flat ahead of payrolls.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities barely budged on Thursday as investors were mostly sidelined ahead of Friday's key employment figures.
Pass-through yield spreads traded in a very narrow range and activity was thin, traders said.
"It's been very, very quiet. We're in a very narrow range," said one pass-through trader at a large U.S. investment bank.
Many market players refrained from taking positions ahead of the U.S. Labor Department's May report on jobs, set for release on Friday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, another trader said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent issues were off 1/32 at 99-27/32, yielding 98 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae were down 2/32 at 99-25/32, and Freddie Mac paper was off 1/32 at 99-30/32.
The five-year Treasury note was even at 6.49 percent, while the 10-year note was up 2/32 to yield 6.62 percent.

On average, 22 economists in a Reuters poll forecast that payrolls rose to 219,000 in May from 142,000 in April. They projected the unemployment rate crept up to 5.0 percent in May from 4.9 percent in the previous month.
